hints: XOR is big when the two numbers disagree in their highest bits. Winning a higher bit beats every lower bit combined. How could you greedily chase disagreement from the top bit down?

Build a binary trie of the numbers, inserting bits from bit 30 down to bit 0. For each number, walk the trie and at every level prefer the child with the opposite bit; if it exists, that bit of the XOR is 1.

1. Create a root node with two children (bit 0 and bit 1).
  2. For each x: insert its bits from 30 down to 0.
  3. Then walk again from the root: at bit b, want = 1 − (bit of x); if that child exists, add 2b to the value and go there, else take the same-bit child.
  4. Keep the maximum value over all x.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every pair (i, j) and take the largest XOR.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Binary trie with greedy opposite-bit walk; inserting before querying also covers i = j (XOR 0).

explain: Sample [5,9,12,3] (0101, 1001, 1100, 0011). When we query 3 = 0011 after the others are inserted: at bit 3 we want a 1, and 9/12 have it, so the XOR gets 8; at bit 2 we want 1, and only 12 continues, so +4; at bits 1 and 0 we want 0 and 12 has 0s, so +2 and +1. Total 15 = 3 XOR 12. Greedy is correct because a higher bit is worth more than all lower bits together. Edge case: inserting x before querying means a single number gives 0, matching i = j being allowed.
recognize: 'Maximum XOR of two numbers from an array' → binary trie, go for the opposite bit from the top.
